graph_diagnosis.summary: Policy restraint, inflation progress, and consumer sentiment provide limited reusable equity-return context.
weaknesses: All realized-index and option links are excluded.
Target support is indirect and requires current inflation, rate, earnings, and risk verification.

search_factors.why_search: Policy restraint affects discount rates and risk appetite.
Disinflation can improve expected policy conditions.
Sentiment can support consumption and risk appetite.
Market reaction around inflation can reveal risk appetite.

checkpoints.mechanism: Restrictive policy conditions influence equity discount rates.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Rate futures and bond yields confirm policy restraint.

checkpoints.mechanism: Disinflation can reduce expected discount-rate pressure.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Inflation cooling is broad and sustained.

checkpoints.mechanism: Improved sentiment can support risk appetite.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Sentiment aligns with consumption and market breadth.

checkpoints.mechanism: Risk appetite can reverse if inflation or policy uncertainty rises.

checkpoints.factor: Discount rates, inflation, and risk appetite
checkpoints.mechanism: Policy expectations, inflation progress, sentiment, and risk appetite combine to determine S&P 500 direction.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Verify current inflation, rate futures, earnings breadth, and risk appetite.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Disinflation can ease expected policy restraint and discount-rate pressure.
Sentiment can support equities unless risk appetite reverses.

alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare rate futures with inflation and volatility measures.

forecast_audit_questions: Do rate futures confirm easier conditions?
